children: OTTAWA--Household net worth in Canada rose in the second quarter, and the stock of credit-market debt as a share of after-tax household income recorded its biggest drop in nearly two years, Statistics Canada said Friday.

The net worth of Canadian households rose 2.9% on an unadjusted basis in the second quarter to surpass the threshold of 19 trillion Canadian dollars (US$13.735 trillion), powered by gains in the equity markets. Household liabilities, mostly mortgages and nonmortgage debt, climbed 1.3%

The closely watched ratio of credit-market debt to after-tax income rose slightly on an unadjusted basis in the April-to-June period, to 175.06%. The data agency noted, however, that on a seasonally adjusted basis, that ratio declined to 176.4% from 178.6%, marking the largest drop since the third quarter of 2024. Income grew at over twice the pace of debt in that period, Statistics Canada said.
As a result, the debt-service ratio also fell to 14.52% in the second quarter.

Second-quarter data measuring gross domestic product indicated that after-tax household income grew due to increases in wages, and higher transfers from government--reflecting new measures to help Canadians deal with higher food prices. The household savings rate also increased in the second quarter.
